title: On the Four-Loop Higgs--Gluon Form Factor in Nonlocal Quantum Field Theory
abstract: In particle physics the virtual N$^3$LO contribution to gluon-fusion Higgs production in the Standard Model requires four-loop multi-scale QCD amplitudes that in dimensional regularization are dominated by singular integral reduction and difficult master-integral evaluations. In this note we show that a nonlocal UV completion makes each fixed-order four-loop Feynman diagram fully convergent in four dimensions while keeping the analytic structure needed for Lehmann-Symanzik-Zimmermann (LSZ) reduction formula. For gluon-fusion $gg\!\to\!H$ we derive a closed form Schwinger-parameter representation where all loop-momentum integrals are performed analytically and thus leaving finite parameter integrals viable for direct numerical evaluation without needing the usual UV subtractions. This method heps to isolate the collider-hard contribution as a convergent four-loop form factor. The strong coupling then is defined by a finite normalization condition in the entire-function regularization scheme and it is related to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ coupling by finite matching where after this matching, the regulator-dependent corrections decouple in the local limit $E_M\!\to\!\infty$.
summary: This paper develops a novel technique using nonlocal quantum field theory to calculate the four-loop Higgs--Gluon form factor, a notoriously difficult quantity in QCD. By introducing a specific regulator, the authors render the previously divergent integrals absolutely convergent in four dimensions. This provides a calculable, UV-finite building block for high-precision predictions of Higgs physics at colliders.
main_problem: The paper addresses the formidable challenge of calculating the virtual N$^3$LO contribution to Higgs production via gluon fusion in the Standard Model, which involves highly complex, multi-scale, four-loop QCD amplitudes.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that employing a nonlocal UV completion allows the calculation of the four-loop Higgs--Gluon form factor to become fully convergent in four dimensions, yielding a closed-form, finite parameter representation.
method: The core method involves using an entire-function regulator in the background-field formalism, which transforms UV-divergent loop integrals into absolutely convergent Gaussian integrals solvable via Schwinger parameterization.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Higgs boson production from gluon fusion ($gg 	o H$) within the framework of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). The theoretical tool employed is a nonlocal Quantum Field Theory providing a UV completion.
key_observables: The regulated four-loop Higgs--Gluon form factor ($F_{ggH}$), and the strong coupling constant ($\alpha_s$).
important_parameters: The regulator scale ($E_M$), the Higgs mass ($m_H$), and the top quark mass ($m_t$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes the regulator function is 'admissible' and that the final physical result requires a separate, finite matching procedure to relate the non-local coupling to the standard $\overline{	ext{MS}}$ coupling.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the difficulty of the N3LO calculation. It then introduces the nonlocal regulator to achieve UV convergence, deriving a closed-form Schwinger-parameter representation for the loop integrals. Finally, it details the necessary finite matching procedure to relate the calculated form factor to the standard $\overline{	ext{MS}}$ prediction.
why_interesting: The methodology of using nonlocal regulators to tame UV divergences in perturbative calculations is a powerful, general technique applicable to any high-order calculation in quantum field theory, potentially simplifying complex calculations in other areas of particle physics.
